_notes: 23 pages. A payer/partner-facing sales deck rather than a fundraise: clinical outcomes, press quotes, a large payer logo wall, service markets and a team page. Rich in outcome percentages, empty on company financials - no revenue, no round, no stage, no HQ. The only investor the deck names is Paul Jacobs, labelled 'Chairman & Founding Investor' on the team slide (p23); the other board members are not stated to have invested, and the deck states no date of its own (the footer carries only a 2020 copyright line).

one_liner.value: Home-centric primary care proven to improve outcomes, delight patients and lower healthcare costs

users.unit: house calls and telehealth visits delivered

expected_flags.note: three revenue models are described (full risk, value-based PCP cap, fee-for-service) but no revenue, margin or contract value figure appears in 23 slides
no round size, valuation, stage or use of funds; the deck has no ask slide
HQ is never stated; the markets slide lists service cities (DC, NYC, Chicago, Southern CA, Seattle, Atlanta, Houston, Charlotte) only

'Who is Heal' slide claims 71% reduction in avoidable ER visits and 28% reduction in admissions; the value-based-care results slide later gives 27% reduction in ER visits and 27% reduction in hospital admissions, with no reconciliation of population or period
'Every dollar invested in effective primary care saves $13 in total healthcare costs' presented as a headline with no source or derivation
'$88MM healthcare cost savings for leading employers and insurance partners' given with no period, no member base and no method; '200K house calls and telehealth visits' likewise has no time frame
